title: A PUBLICATION (L3) — the terminal deliverable a route is trying to reach
_role: Every route's end goal is a paper. Without this collection the model could say what a route WAS and what BLOCKED it, and could not say what it was FOR -- the endpoint existed only for routes lucky enough to already have a file, and vanished for the ones that had not been written yet. That asymmetry made an unwritten paper indistinguishable from no paper at all, which is the state most of the portfolio is actually in.
_why_this_is_a_graph_row_and_L4_is_not: ARCHITECTURE §3 keeps L3/L4 as DOCUMENTS on the grounds that copying a file's title into JSON creates a second home for a fact the file already owns. That reasoning is intact and is why `title` is absent here whenever `document` is set -- the row POINTS at the file and the renderer reads the title back out of its frontmatter. What the reasoning did not cover is a paper that does not exist yet: an unwritten publication has no file, so it has no other home, and leaving it unmodelled is what made 'no endpoint' and 'endpoint not yet written' render identically.

state.description: ⛔ NO VAGUE STATES. The question this answers is 'how much of this paper exists?', and it is deliberately NOT a quality grade -- `drafted` says a draft file exists, never that the draft is good. Whether the science is publishable is `target_venue` against each route's own `readiness.attainable_today`, which is a different question with a different owner. `posted_preprint` sits between `complete_unposted` and `posted`: the document has an outside reader and a citable identifier (a preprint server, e.g. Qeios or aiXiv) but has not reached its `target_venue`'s final placement -- see the `posted` property for the record of that act.

posted.description: REQUIRED when `state` is `posted_preprint` or `posted`; absent otherwise. The record of the one act that gives this document an outside reader -- CLAUDE.md §6: a submission is the only moment anything here reaches an outside reader, and every identifier here is transcribed from the publisher's own record, never from an announcement (CLAUDE.md §7).

posted_by.description: Who actually posted it, and whether an agent grant was used -- CLAUDE.md §3: publish only the paper trimcrae named, as the paper it is, per act.

_evidence.description: How the fields above were read -- primary source, never the announcement (CLAUDE.md §7).

target_venue.description: The form this deliverable is AIMED at. Same closed vocabulary as `route.readiness.attainable_today` on purpose: the two are meant to be compared, and a route whose readiness sits below its endpoint's venue is the honest statement of the gap. Ordered but NOT a ladder -- an experimental_proposal is a different output from a journal submission, not a lesser one.

document.description: The file, when one exists. NULL is the whole point of this collection: a paper nobody has started still has an endpoint, a claim and a reason it is unwritten. The file's own frontmatter owns its title -- nothing here copies it -- and check_pointers verifies the path exists.

working_title.description: REQUIRED when `document` is null and FORBIDDEN when it is not. An unwritten paper needs a handle a human can talk about; a written one already has one in its frontmatter, and a second copy here would be the one-fact-two-homes bug.

what_it_would_claim.description: REQUIRED on every row, written so a reader can disagree with it. ⭐ THIS IS THE FIELD THAT MAKES AN UNWRITTEN PAPER REAL: if the one sentence the paper would put into the field's record cannot be stated, there is no endpoint -- there is an activity. It is a statement of what the work would ESTABLISH, never a claim of efficacy, safety, a therapeutic window or clinical readiness, and lint_claims.py binds the generated view exactly as it binds the manuscript.

why_not_written.description: REQUIRED while `state` is `unwritten` or `outlined`. Names what is actually missing -- a result, a decision, a person, or only the writing. 'Only the writing' is a legitimate and important answer: it distinguishes a paper that is blocked from one that is merely unstarted, and the portfolio contains both.

blocked_by.description: Blockers that hold up the PAPER rather than the science. Usually a subset of what its routes inherit: a route can be blocked on a capability while its paper is publishable as an honest negative, and that difference is the portfolio's main source of publishable work.

companion_of.description: A deliverable that ships WITH another rather than alone -- an experimental proposal sent alongside the preprint that motivates it. Records the pairing without merging two things that have different readers.

outcome_potential.description: What this endpoint could still do FOR A PATIENT. ⛔ A JUDGEMENT, NOT A DERIVED FACT — recorded as data so it can be argued with one row at a time instead of hiding inside a score. `live_positive`: could still report a positive that a wet lab or a clinic could act on. `negative_or_methods`: the content is a known negative, a failure record, a closure or an instrument contribution — valuable, and not a treatment lead. `horizon_scan`: parked on a capability nobody has.

outcome_potential_why.description: One line justifying the classification, written so a reader can disagree with it.

patient_path.description: HOW a result here reaches a patient, and HOW BIG the next step is for whoever has to take it. ⚠ A JUDGEMENT, recorded as data so it can be argued with one row at a time. Replaces the boolean `wet_lab_test_named` (2026-08-09), which failed in both directions: it could not distinguish a test somebody had ALREADY RUN from one a lab could pick up, and it scored zero for the one paper that reaches a patient with NO laboratory at all — whose own note read 'which is why the flag is False and not a demerit' while the flag was costing it the single largest term in the score. `prebuilt_bench`: constructs, controls and kill criteria exist, or it bolts onto an assay already running. `no_bench_needed`: actionable now by sponsors, registries or tool-builders. `named_bench`: a specific decisive experiment a lab would still have to build. `clinical_adoption`: reaches a patient through practice change. `none`: no concrete next actor — which for a negative is the honest value, not a demerit.

unit.description: What size of publishable unit this actually is. ⚠ ADDED 2026-08-09 because the board had no way to answer 'is that even a paper?' — trimcrae asked it of PUB-STRATEGY-ARCH, which sits third in the ranking at 1,958 words, under a third the length of the next shortest endpoint. A short report is not a lesser contribution; it is a different object, and a ranking that hides the difference invites exactly that question.

next_act.description: The one remaining act on this publication that is TRIMCRAE'S and only his — posting, submitting, depositing, minting. Read by research/autonomy/ready_to_post.py, which owns the closed vocabulary in its `HIS_ACTS` map; that map is the single home for the list and is deliberately NOT duplicated here as an enum. ⚠ ready_to_post.py fails CLOSED on an unrecognised value: the paper is silently dropped from his queue rather than flagged, so a typo here reads exactly like 'nothing is waiting'. Clearing this field is what records that he has done it.

next_venue.description: The venue `next_act` would be performed at. Passed to publish_bar.evaluate as `venue`, which defaults to 'aixiv' when absent — so a paper waiting on a non-aiXiv venue MUST set this or it is graded against the wrong bar.

_next_act_why.description: Prose: why this act is his rather than the loop's. Underscore-prefixed because nothing reads it — it is for the next session, which otherwise sees a queue entry with no reason attached.

route_endpoint.description: A route's `publication` field — where this route's work ends up. Exactly one endpoint per route: a route whose output is split across two papers has not been analysed, it has been described.

role.description: `primary` — the paper is ABOUT this route. `contributing` — the route supplies a section, a control, a supplement or a disclosed limitation. `context` — the route is cited to establish the landscape and is explicitly NOT this program's contribution. The third exists because two routes here are clinical-evidence synthesis whose own registers say so, and promoting them to contributions would overstate what was done.

contribution.description: What THIS route puts into that paper. Not a restatement of the route's purpose — the question is what the paper loses if this route is dropped.
